results.answer: The Best B.Tech Project Awards during the ceremony held on 15th May 2026 were presented by Prof. N. P. Padhi, the Director of MNIT Jaipur. He was accompanied by Dr. Rajeev Kumar Dohare, Head of the Department of Chemical Engineering, and Prof. (HAG) S. P. Chaurasia at the event [1].

sources.text: Malaviya National Institute of Technology Jaipur Department of Chemical Engineering B.Tech. Project Award Ceremony-Cum Farewell The Department of Chemical Engineering , in association with the student chapter of IIChEJRC, MNIT Jaipur, proudly organized the B.Tech Project Award Ceremony-cum-Farewell on 15th May 2026 to recognize and celebrate the outstanding innovation, dedication, and project work demonstrated by our students. The awards were graciously presented by Prof. N. P . Padhi, Director, MNIT Jaipur , in the esteemed presence of Dr. Rajeev Kumar Dohare, Head of the Department of Chemical Engineering, and Prof. (HAG) S. P. Chaurasia. The occasion was further enriched by the presence of our distinguished external examiners, Prof. Anand Kishore Kola and Dr. Bharatkumar K. Modhera, whose valuable insights, guidance, and encouragement added great significance to the event. The Best B.Tech Project Awards were conferred upon: • Sumit Singh, Harshveer Singh Chauhan, and Naeem Ahmad, mentored by Dr. Dipalay Datta. • Sujal Prakash Rathore, Manish Singh, and Yash Bhuria , mentored by Dr. Pooja Jangir. This ceremony not only recognized the exceptional achievements of our students but also highlighted the department’s commitment to fostering innovation, research excellence, and industry-relevant education.

results.answer: For the Ph.D. program in the academic session 2016-17, international students (specifically those from countries other than SAARC) are required to pay an additional tuition fee of **US $4000**. Students from SAARC countries have a reduced tuition fee of **US $2000**. results.question: What is the mandatory criterion for Ph.D. admission with scholarship support in Engineering and Sciences?
results.answer: The mandatory criterion for Ph.D. admission with scholarship support in Engineering and Sciences is that a GATE score is required. Specifically, the GATE score must have been obtained within the past three years, or the candidate must have completed their respective Master's degree with a valid GATE score [1].

results.answer:
For M.Sc. Full-time students in the Even Semester, the fee structure differs between General Category and SC/ST students primarily in the Tuition Fee part.

  - Tuition Fee: ₹7500
  - Total for Admission/Tuition: ₹9000
  
- **SC/ST Students**:
  - Admission Processing Fee: ₹1500
  - Tuition Fee: ₹0 (exempt)
  - Total for Admission/Tuition: ₹1500

Thus, the significant difference is that SC/ST students do not pay the Tuition Fee, resulting in a total fee of ₹10815 for SC/ST students compared to ₹18315 for General/OBC students [1][2][3].

results.question: What is the adopted formula for converting CGPA into percentage marks at MNIT Jaipur?
results.answer:
The adopted formula for converting CGPA into percentage marks at MNIT Jaipur is:

**Percentage Marks = CGPA x 10**

This formula was established as per a decision taken by the Senate during its 34th meeting held on 10th February 2016, which superseded the previous order [1].

results.question: What is required from Ph.D. students before they can convert from full-time to part-time status?
results.answer:
Before Ph.D. students can convert from full-time to part-time status, they are required to submit a consent letter from their employer if they are working more than 70 km from Jaipur. This consent letter indicates the employer's permission for the student to pursue their Ph.D. part-time. Additionally, the following conditions must be met:

1. The student must have satisfied the requirement for the minimum period of residency as a full-time student.
2. Students converting from full-time to part-time are not allowed to submit their Ph.D. thesis until at least one year has passed from the date of the consent letter or the minimum residency period for part-time students, whichever is later.
3. They must also fulfill any minimum attendance requirement as outlined in the PG regulations or any established by their respective supervisors or the DREC [1].

results.question: What national examinations allow candidates to waive the written test for Ph.D. admission?
results.answer:
Candidates can waive the written test for Ph.D. admission at the institute if they have cleared the following national examinations with a scholarship:

1. UGC NET
2. CSIR
3. DST Inspire

Additionally, any other national examination offering a scholarship may also qualify. These candidates are still required to appear for an interview [1].

results.question: What does the New Education Policy recommend regarding internships for UG and PG students?
results.answer: The New Education Policy recommends that internships be an integral part of the curriculum for both UG and PG students, emphasizing practical exposure and vocational training. It aims to enhance graduates' employability by providing hands-on experience and facilitating a smooth transition from education to industry. Industrial internships are encouraged for a duration of six months to a maximum of one year, with specific recommendations for their implementation during the academic program [1].

In accordance with the approval granted by the Senate in its 41st meeting held on is"March 2021 under Item No. 41-3.1. The guidelines for industrial internships of UG and PG students are as under: Internship guidelines for UG students The New Education Policy strongly recommends that practical exposure, vocational trammg, internships be integral part of the curriculum. This would produce graduates who have hands on working and problem-solving experience. This will help in their seamless transition from the Institute to the Industry. The employability of the students who undergo internship in reputed companies will be high as Industry would get work force in line with their requirements. In order to encourage Industry Institute interaction and to impart practical exposure to the students the committee strongly recommends Industrial internships to the students for a period of six months to a maximum of one year. DUGC of the department shall recommend all the cases of industrial internships and ensure that the following norms are observed. 1. Internship in VII Semester only (can also be in continuation of summer internship for 2 months after VI Semester) a. Completion of all courses up to VI Semester without any backlogs b. Course waiver of 16 credits in lieu of internship. 2. Internship in VITISemester only: a.' Completion of all courses up to VII Semester without any backlogs

ATTENDANCE, ABSENCE AND LEAVE 10.1 Attendance Requirement All the undergraduate students are expected to be present in every lecture, tutorial/studio, practical or drawing classes scheduled for them. An undergraduate student must have a minimum attendance of seventy five percent (75%) of the total number of classes including lectures, tutorials and practical held in a course in order to be eligible to appear in the End - Term Examination for that course. A student should meet the above attendance requirement irrespective of the number of days he/she is on medical and/or other leave for any reason whatsoever. Attendance of the students shall be monitored and displayed during a semester as per the guidelines approved by the SUGB. The names of the s tudents who have remained absent with or without leave, for more than 25% of the actual classes held in a course will be intimated by the Course Coordinator to the Convener, DUGC/First Year Class Coordina tor on the last teaching day of the semester. The consolidated list of all such students for all the courses in a parti cular semester will be displayed on the notice board of the Department/Academic Section. The list of such students shall also be forwarded to the Dean, Academics.
